html:
The Bidai, who called themselves Quasmigdo, were a Native American people of eastern Texas, living along the Trinity River between the Caddo to the north and the Atakapa to the south. Their name comes from a Caddo word meaning "brushwood". Their language may have been related to Atakapa.

They farmed, hunted and gathered, and traded with the French and Spanish in the 1700s. Spain founded missions for them and their neighbours in the 1740s, part of its effort to hold Spanish Texas against the French. An epidemic in 1776 and 1777 killed about half of them. The survivors later joined other peoples, and by the mid 1800s the Bidai had vanished as a separate people.
